title: Professional Ethics & Liabilities of Auditors
outcomes: Apply the Code of Ethics, threats and NOCLAR.
Explain membership and certificate of practice rules.
Identify misconduct under the Schedules and disciplinary procedure.
Apply the Guidelines on Ethical Issues, 2026 and tax audit limits.

meta.exam_tip: Answer ethics cases in four steps: provision, facts, analysis, conclusion.

concepts.title: Code of Ethics: principles, threats and NOCLAR
body: The ICAI Code of Ethics (based on the IESBA Code) sets fundamental principles — integrity, objectivity, competence with due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour — and a conceptual framework to identify, evaluate and address threats (self-interest, self-review, advocacy, familiarity, intimidation).
Independence of mind and in appearance is required for audit and assurance engagements; safeguards or refusal apply where threats cannot be reduced to an acceptable level.

NOCLAR (non-compliance with laws and regulations) provisions guide professional accountants who become aware of actual or suspected non-compliance: understand the matter, discuss with management and TCWG, consider further action including disclosure to authorities where appropriate, and document.
concepts.analogy: Principles plus a threat-safeguard method govern every ethical decision.
concepts.work: A CA learning of a client's environmental violation follows NOCLAR steps.

concepts.title: Membership, certificate of practice and deemed practice
body: A person becomes a member on registration with ICAI; disabilities include being under 21, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, conviction of certain offences, or removal for misconduct. Members are associates (ACA) or fellows (FCA). Names may be removed (death, request, non-payment of fees, misconduct) and restored.

A member in practice must hold a certificate of practice; members are deemed to be in practice if they hold themselves out, offer services, or render professional services including those permitted by the Council (e.g. management consultancy).
Companies cannot engage in accountancy; practising members cannot use designations other than CA (except permitted ones) and must follow rules on branch offices and KYC norms for clients.
concepts.analogy: The certificate of practice defines who can practise as a CA.
concepts.work: A CA offering tax services publicly without a certificate of practice breaches the Act.

concepts.title: Misconduct under the Schedules and disciplinary procedure
body: Section 22 defines professional or other misconduct by reference to the Schedules. First Schedule: Part I (members in practice), Part II (members in service), Part III (members generally), Part IV (other misconduct). Second Schedule: Part I (in practice), Part II (generally), Part III (other misconduct) — graver matters such as gross negligence and false certification.

Examples: allowing a non-CA to practise in one's name; sharing fees with non-members; soliciting clients; advertising beyond guidelines; accepting audit without communicating with the previous auditor in writing; certifying without proper examination; disclosing client information without consent.

Disciplinary mechanism: Director (Discipline) forms a prima facie opinion; First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline and Second Schedule or both to the Disciplinary Committee; penalties include reprimand, removal and fines, with appeals to the Appellate Authority.
concepts.analogy: Know which Schedule, which part and which clause.
concepts.work: Not writing to the previous auditor before accepting is professional misconduct.

concepts.title: Guidelines on Ethical Issues, 2026 and self-regulatory measures
body: The Guidelines on Ethical Issues, 2026 include: employees must exercise due diligence; practising members must maintain cash book, ledger and bill register; not accepting audit where the previous auditor's undisputed audit fee is unpaid (except sick units and insolvency cases); a ceiling of 40 company audit assignments per practising partner (excluding OPCs and dormant companies); and restrictions on non-audit fees for statutory audits of PSUs, government companies, listed companies and public companies with turnover of ₹250 crore or more.

The Limit on Number of Tax Audits Guidelines, 2025 cap tax audits at 60 per practising partner per financial year, excluding audits under section 44AB clauses (c), (d) and (e) for 44AE, 44ADA and 44AD cases; revised reports and branches do not add assignments.

Recommended self-regulatory measures cover branch and joint audits, ratio of qualified to unqualified staff, disclosure of interests in other firms, and receiving audit fees through banking channels or digital modes. Auditors also face civil liability (negligence), criminal liability (false statements) and Companies Act penalties.
concepts.analogy: Specific numeric limits are favourite exam traps.
concepts.work: A three-partner firm can hold up to 120 company audits under the 2026 Guidelines.

illustrations.title: Is this misconduct?
illustrations.q: Decide: (a) CA A accepts audit of a company whose previous auditor's undisputed audit fee is unpaid; the company's net worth is positive. (b) CA B allows his non-CA brother to sign certificates in B's name. (c) CA C, in practice, does not keep books of account for his practice since his income is below section 44AA limits. (d) CA D discloses client information to a regulator as required by law.

head: Case
Position
rows: Misconduct under the 2026 Guidelines (Chapter IV) — exemption only for sick units or insolvency cases
Misconduct — First Schedule Part I, clause (1): allowing a non-CA to practise in his name
Misconduct — Guidelines require cash book, ledger and bill register regardless of 44AA
Not misconduct — disclosure required by law is permitted

jobs.title: Ethics compliance at a CA firm
jobs.situation: A growing firm with five partners and many tax audits.
steps: Maintain register of company and tax audit assignments.
Check previous auditor communication and fees before acceptance.
Keep proper books of the practice.
Review non-audit fees for restricted clients.
jobs.takeaway: Ethical limits must be tracked like any other compliance.

summary: Code of Ethics: five principles, threats, NOCLAR.
First and Second Schedule; Board of Discipline vs Disciplinary Committee.
2026 Guidelines: 40 company audits per partner; books; unpaid fees.
remember: Legal disclosure is not a breach of confidentiality.

viva.model: Guidance in the Code of Ethics on responding to actual or suspected non-compliance with laws and regulations, including discussion and possible disclosure to authorities.

viva.q: Who is deemed to be in practice?
viva.model: A member who holds out as a practising CA, offers or renders professional services, or performs services permitted by the Council.

viva.q: How are First and Second Schedule matters handled?
viva.model: First Schedule matters go to the Board of Discipline; Second Schedule or combined matters go to the Disciplinary Committee.

viva.q: What are the audit assignment limits under current guidelines?
viva.model: Forty company audits and sixty tax audits a year per practising partner, with specified exclusions.

viva.q: Name auditors' liabilities beyond ICAI discipline.
viva.model: Civil liability for negligence, criminal liability for false statements and penalties under the Companies Act.
